content:
Maria: Heads-up — RFC follow-up: I'm proposing a small refactor we call the 'token-broker' to centralize admission/fairness decisions. Draft: https://rfc.internal/token-broker (short summary below)

Kevin: tl;dr?

Maria: Move admission logic out of every edge proxy into a lightweight broker service that holds ephemeral credit state, enforces fairness windows, and exposes a tiny admit/check API. Edges become simple forwarders + local cache.

Dave: Why not keep it in edge proxies? single hop fewer bytes -> lower p99

Maria: Good Q. Edge-only has duplication and inconsistent fairness across regions. Broker allows stronger cross-tenant fairness and easier rollout of new abuse signals. We accept ~1-2ms extra RTT for majority of requests; critical low-latency paths can short-circuit to local admit in fail-fast mode.

Jess: Sounds like a potential SPOF. What's the HA plan?

Maria: Broker will be regional, multi-replica with leaderless consensus for credit updates. Design includes sticky local cache with short TTL + optimistic admission so edges can function if broker is unreachable.

Kevin: Storage for credits? Redis? Postgres?

Dave: We should avoid per-token DB hits. prefer in-memory stores with periodic persistence. Redis primary + write-ahead to durable store for audits. We can shard by tenant id.

Jess: How do we handle bursty tenants who try to game fairness by opening many small connections?

Maria: Broker will expose multi-dimension quotas: tenant, API-key, and aggregated org. Admission policy supports leaky-bucket + dynamic penalty scaling. Also global abuse detectors feed score adjustments that reduce effective credit.

Kevin: What about Dedicated / Private customers? They might not want central broker in our control.

Maria: For Dedicated we run a tenant-local broker in the customer's VPC. For Private/on-prem we ship a broker binary/helm chart. The API surface is identical so code paths are reusable.

sre-bot: Note: add health probes and per-node admission latency histograms to the runbook.

Dave: Migration plan? No one wants ripple failure during cutover.

Maria: Phased rollout: 1) opt-in broker for non-critical tenants 2) edge caches + observe divergence 3) default-broker for 10% traffic (canary) 4) progressively increase while monitoring fairness/latency/err rates 5) fallback toggle per region.

Kevin: Metrics we need to add before canary: per-tenant admit latency, broker availability, cache hit rate, divergence count (edge admit != broker admit), and downstream error correlation.

Jess: Agreed. Also audit log of penalty adjustments and explicit reason codes for denials.

Maria: Example admit API sketch (proto):

```
service TokenBroker {
  rpc CheckAdmit(CheckRequest) returns (CheckReply);
}
message CheckRequest {
  string tenant_id = 1;
  string api_key = 2;
  int32 tokens = 3; // requested tokens
  map<string,string> meta = 4; // e.g., model, region
}
message CheckReply {
  bool allowed = 1;
  int32 tokens_granted = 2;
  string reason = 3; // short code
  int64 expiry_ms = 4; // cache hint
}
```

Dave: We should include a bulk check endpoint to amortize RPCs for batched clients.

Maria: yea bulk support planned. Also a streaming admission stream for high-throughput internal services.

Kevin: Concern: latency SLO will shift from edge p99 -> edge+broker p99. We need to model impact on tail. Have we simulated heatmaps?

Maria: Perf sim results in RFC: for typical 99.9 percentile request sizes we see +0.8ms median, +3-4ms p99 in worst case, but able to reduce heavy-tail with broker-side batching improvements. Sim code: https://staging/sim/token-broker-sim

Jess: For offline audits we need durable records of credits consumed per minute. Agree on WAL approach. Make sure PII-free.

sre-bot: Ops checklist: playbook for broker-leader-failover, runbook for cache-staleness alerts, circuit-breaker thresholds.

Kevin: What about fairness policy language? Do we hardcode heuristic or expose a policy DSL?

Maria: Short term: heuristic config + weight adjustments via feature flags. Long term: small policy DSL (jsonnet-ish) to express bucket weights, decay windows, and exception rules.

Dave: Is there a throttling backpressure signal to clients? We should return a structured 429 with retry-after and quota metadata so clients can implement backoff.

Maria: yes 429 body will include: current_tokens, granted_tokens, penalty_score, suggested_cooldown. Also a machine-readable reason.

Kevin: Telemetry tags: tenant_id, api_key_level, model_family, route, broker_node, cache_hit bool. Keep tag cardinality reasonable.

Jess: Security: make sure edge <-> broker mTLS, auth via signed short-lived tokens. KMS to rotate. Dedicated/private customers can bring their own KMS.

Maria: Open questions for the RFC follow-up: - broker API backpressure semantics (sync vs async admit) - exact cache TTL heuristic per route - penalty scaling curve (linear vs exponential) - audit storage retention and archival policy

Dave: Can we get a short spike next sprint to prototype the redis-backed broker and measure p99 impact?

Maria: I'll file a spike ticket and assign. Also want a small runbook doc attached to the RFC.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/token-broker-spike -> staging

Kevin: Thanks — leaving comments on the RFC. tagging @sre for ops review.

Jess: I'm +1 for the spike. We should schedule a 30min sync after spike results.

Maria: Cool, will update RFC with responses here. Thanks all. :raised_hands:
